correctness_confidence.basis: All algebraic identities, SRG parameter equations, Kneser incidence factorizations, binary/ternary polar bounds, Sturm root isolations, and sporadic minor determinants are mathematically sound. Lean 4.36.0 compiles all 20 scalar theorems warning-free without sorry or Classical.choice, and the zero-float Python suite verifies all graphs, ranks, minors, and annihilating polynomials via 16 SHA-256 certificates.

novelty.basis: The self-contained primal-dual SRG collapse proof, Veronese rank bound for I+A on ternary polar graphs, complete shifted-adjacency p|(m-4) dichotomy for KG(m,2), and zero-float Sturm certification of primal Schrijver bounds on non-SRGs are crisp syntheses. Core SRG collapse and p-rank phenomena build directly on Schrijver (1979), Brouwer-van Eijl (1992), and Peeters (1996), now properly cited.

reproducibility.basis: Exemplary two-layer zero-trust artifacts: ShannonCapacityPolarHaemers.lean compiles cleanly under Lean 4.36.0 with -DwarningAsError=true and zero external dependencies; the pure-stdlib Python verifier passes an AST zero-float audit (no floats, /, **, or limit_denominator) and emits 16 deterministic SHA-256 certificates matching MANIFEST.json; 56 adversarial pytest checks independently validate edge cases.

rigor.basis: All proofs in the revised manuscript are complete and self-contained. The Abstract and Section 5 transparently separate Lean 4.36.0 scalar Int/Nat algebraic kernels from Python Layer 2 matrix/Sturm verification, Theorem 3(c) includes the universal rank-subadditivity bound ruling out non-optimal shifts for all primes p > 11, and V_2 spanning plus k_bar > 0 on NO_{nsq}(3,p) are explicitly proved.

significance.basis: Provides a clean, verified algebraic benchmark atlas separating alpha, Theta, minrk_{F_p}, real rank, and theta'=theta across canonical graph families, alongside a reusable zero-float Sturm method for primal Schrijver lower bounds on non-SRGs. While valuable for extremal combinatorics and verified optimization, it does not resolve major open capacities such as Theta(HS).

summary: This revised manuscript proves three exact algebraic-combinatorial theorems separating Shannon capacity Theta(G), characteristic-p Haemers bounds, real shifted-adjacency rank, and Lovasz-Schrijver bounds (theta, theta') across strongly regular and polar graphs. Theorem 1 gives an unconditional primal-dual proof of theta'=theta on all SRGs and establishes an O(m) << Theta(3^m) << Theta(9^m/4) hierarchy on NO_eps(2m+1,3), an F_3 discriminant-parity obstruction (alpha=2m vs. rank 2m+1), and a Veronese bound for I+A. Theorem 2 proves the shifted-adjacency dichotomy min_{c!=0} rank_{F_p}(cI+A(KG(m,2))) = m-1 iff p|(m-4) for all m>=5 and primes p. Theorem 3 derives exponential F_2-Haemers gaps on binary polar complements, zero-float Sturm-certified primal theta' lower bounds on non-SRGs NO_{sq/nsq}(3,p), and a sporadic SRG atlas highlighting Higman-Sims (F_2 rank 100 vs. odd-prime rank 23). The revision resolves all prior objections: Lean 4.36.0 vs. zero-float Python verification scopes are clearly separated, Theorem 3(c) supplies the universal rank-subadditivity bound for all shifts and primes, V_2 spanning and k_bar>0 are explicitly proved, and Brouwer-van Eijl (1992) and Peeters (1996) are properly cited.
strengths: Self-contained primal-dual proof of universal Schrijver-Lovasz collapse theta'(G) = theta(G) on all strongly regular graphs without symmetry or association-scheme assumptions.

Sharp analysis of NO_eps(2m+1,3) yielding a three-way exponential hierarchy (O(m) vs. Theta(3^m) vs. Theta(9^m/4)), exact F_3 discriminant-parity obstruction (alpha = 2m < 2m+1), and Veronese factorization bounding rank_{F_3}(I+A).
Complete if-and-only-if shifted-adjacency collapse criterion p|(m-4) for Kneser graphs KG(m,2) across all m >= 5 and all primes p, with exact control of non-collapsing shifts c != -1 (mod p).
Zero-float rational Sturm root isolation certifying primal Schrijver theta' lower bounds on non-SRGs NO_{sq/nsq}(3,p), including exact equality theta'=theta=19/5 on NO_{sq}(3,29).

Constructive Witt-design S(3,6,22) verification, 23x23 Schur-complement minor (det = 2^22 * 3^2), and rank-subadditivity proof pinning minrk_{F_p}^{shift}(HS) = 23 for every odd prime p >= 3 versus (I+A)^2 = I (rank 100) over F_2.

Transparent two-layer verification stack: 20 constructive Lean 4.36.0 scalar theorems (0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice), AST-audited zero-float Python verifier, 16 SHA-256 certificates, and 56 adversarial tests.
weaknesses: Core phenomena such as SRG theta'=theta collapse and p-ranks of triangular/Higman-Sims graphs overlap with classical results (Schrijver 1979, Brouwer-van Eijl 1992, Peeters 1996), though the paper now contextualizes them appropriately.
In Table 1, the Real / Other Rank column for NO^+(2m,2)^c and NO^-(2m,2)^c lists concrete F_2 ranks (7, 9 and 5, 7, 9) rather than real shifted-adjacency ranks (minor presentational note).
strong_novelty_candidates: Veronese quadratic factorization I+A(G) = Phi(U) D Phi(U)^T (mod 3) capping rank_{F_3}(I+A) <= binom(2m+2, 2) on ternary polar graphs (attaining equality 15 at m=2).
Exact arithmetic dichotomy min_{c in F_p^x} rank_{F_p}(cI+A(KG(m,2))) = m-1 <=> p|(m-4) across all primes p and shifts c, highlighting sharp non-collapse at (m,p)=(6,5) despite 5|(m-1).
Zero-float rational Sturm root-isolation certification of primal Schrijver theta' bounds on non-SRGs NO_{sq/nsq}(3,p), including exact equality theta'=theta=19/5 on NO_{sq}(3,29).
